- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion or lagged support.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +1.00 to -0.33), model may misread momentum; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift, especially if price drops >2% from prior.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply 3-period exponential smoothing or use sentiment-weighted average to dampen noise.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is flat, model tends to drift; use 10-day moving average or sentiment-weighted median to anchor forecast.
